index.subtitle: Pick a planet to start your adventure

description_2: Take your first steps with the house
description_3: Learn to share and leave remainders

guided.step_2: How many times does it fit?

feedback.hint_quotient: Think: what number times the divisor gets close without going over?
feedback.hint_product: Multiply the quotient digit by the divisor
feedback.hint_remainder: Subtract the product from the partial number
feedback.hint_bring_down: Bring down the next digit of the dividend
feedback.hint_zero_quotient: Since the number is smaller than the divisor, write 0 and bring down another digit

step_l1_intro: Welcome to your first mission. Today you will learn the basic concepts of division: the dividend, the divisor, the quotient and the remainder. Get ready for liftoff.
step_l1_glossary_intro: Before we divide, meet the characters of this space adventure.
step_l1_glossary_dividend: It is the number we want to share out. It goes inside the division house.
step_l1_glossary_divisor: It is the number we are sharing by. It travels outside, next to the house.
step_l1_glossary_quotient: It is the result of the division: how many times the divisor fits into the dividend. It is written on top.
step_l1_glossary_remainder: It is what is left over when you cannot share everything. When the remainder is 0, the division is exact.
step_l1_guided_1: Divide 8 rockets into 2 ships. Write each digit of the quotient to complete the mission.
step_l1_practice_1: Now it is time to practice. Divide 12 meteors into 3 groups. You can do it!
step_l1_summary: Excellent! You now know the dividend, the divisor, the quotient and the remainder. Keep exploring to divide bigger numbers.
step_l2_intro: In this mission you will learn to divide step by step using the division house.
step_l2_guided_1: Divide 84 ships into 4 squadrons. Take the digits one at a time.
step_l2_practice_1: Now you practice: divide 96 astronauts into 3 space bases.
step_l2_summary: Mission accomplished! Dividing step by step is easier than it looked.
step_l3_intro: Some divisions are not exact. What is left over is called the remainder.
step_l3_guided_1: Divide 23 gems into 4 chests. You will have gems left over: that is the remainder!
step_l3_practice_1: Divide 29 stars into 5 constellations. How many are left over?
step_l3_summary: Great! You can now divide with remainders. Remember: the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
step_l4_intro: Today the divisor has two digits. The idea is the same: keep trying how many times it fits.
step_l4_guided_1: Divide 87 planets into 21 colonies. Try how many times 21 fits.
step_l4_practice_1: Divide 154 probes into 23 teams. Go step by step!
step_l4_summary: Fantastic! With two-digit divisors, keep trying digits one at a time.
step_l5_intro: Sometimes zeros appear in the quotient or numbers have many digits. Here you will learn to master them.
step_l5_guided_1: Divide 1204 moons into 4 satellites. Watch what happens when the first digit is smaller than the divisor.
step_l5_guided_2: Divide 1000 comets into 8 hunters. The zeros in the quotient are important clues.
step_l5_summary: Space mission complete! You now know how to handle the special cases of division.
